study: Attempted-finger classifier on three later dates, and its decisions replayed through a simulated hand
what: A classifier read which finger one person with tetraplegia was attempting to move, from recordings in posterior parietal cortex; its decisions, right and wrong, then drove a simulated hand with 39 muscles at four keys.

of those, presses where the simulated hand struck the key the person had attempted

the same control: commands the simulated hand carried out

why_some_numbers_have_no_macro: Whole numbers below 100, and round numbers that double as percentages or durations elsewhere in the papers, have no macro: the build would otherwise refuse the same digits wherever another section types them as an ordinary number. The papers print them as words or as plain digits; each is listed here with its source so that it can be checked.
limits: One participant; three dates are not three people. The labels are cued attempts, not measured finger movements, and seeing the cue is not separated from attempting the movement.
The classifier needed fifty labelled examples from each date; with none it scored at the chance rate.
The hand is a generic simulated hand, not the participant's. Nothing here was recorded from muscle, nerve or spinal cord.
The replay ran from stored recordings after the fact; it is not live.
The three later dates have now been seen and count as development data for any later work.
credit: Finger_RL, DANDI Archive 000252, version 0.230408.2207 (Guan, Aflalo, Kadlec and Gamez). Hand model: MyoSim; simulator: MuJoCo.
